chunks: As for what Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, from al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Kaysan al-San'ani, who said:
I wrote to Abī al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام asking him about sajdah upon cotton and linen without taqiyyah and without necessity. So he wrote back to me: That is permissible.

So this does not contradict the earlier reports upon which we have compiled, because it is possible that he only permitted it while negating a necessity that reaches the destruction of the soul, even though there may be a lesser necessity than that, such as heat or cold and whatever resembles that, as we have explained.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارَ: narrations or reports used in legal reconciliation
key_terms.الْقُطْنِ: cotton as a material upon which sajdah is discussed
key_terms.الْكَتَّانِ: linen as a material upon which sajdah is discussed
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation for protection under circumstances of risk
key_terms.جَائِزٌ: permissible according to the ruling given
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: necessity or constraining hardship affecting the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is sajdah on cotton and linen permissible in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing sajdah on cotton and linen and reports a written response from Abī al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام permitting it. The compiler then reconciles this report with earlier narrations by explaining that the permission may apply in cases of lesser hardship such as heat or cold, even if not life-threatening necessity.
